entries.title: Leviticus 4:2
segments: Through ignorance; not sensible at the time of doing what was wrong, but becoming convinced of it afterwards.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:3
segments: The priest that is anointed; the high-priest.

According to the sin of the people; or to bring guilt upon the people; for he acted as their representative, and his sin involved them in its consequences. 
 
  For a sin-offering; in the burnt-offering and peace-offering there was an acknowledgment of general sinfulness which needed expiation. But the sin-offering was for particular transgressions of the law. 
 
There is no man or body of men on earth infallible, or perfect.  All are liable to sin, through carelessness, inattention, and the influence of temptation.  All need repentance and pardon through faith in the atonement of Jesus Christ.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:4
segments: Lay his hand upon the bullock's head; solemnly consecreating the victim to God as an offering for sin; thus confessing his own sin, and his desire to have the liability to suffer transferred from himself to the sacrifice of God's appointment.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:6
segments: Seven; a number signifying fulness, completeness.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:12
segments: The whole bullock; except the fat, which was burnt, and the blood.

. 
 
  With fire; a fire made upon the ground for that purpose. 
 
The way in which God pardons sin is suited to make a deep impression of its evil, and lead men to abhor and forsake it.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:15
segments: The elders; their chief men, magistrates, representatives of the people.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:20
segments: Make an atonement--be forgiven; he who, in the spirit of true faith and penitence, presented to God his sin-offering, was saved not only from the temporal punishment of his sin, but also, through the atonement of Christ which this offering typified, from its eternal consequences.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:21
segments: Nations, as well as individuals, may commit great iniquity; and without national repentance, reformation, and pardon through the atonement of Christ, such iniquity will draw down upon them the sore judgments of God.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:26
segments: Rulers and teachers, ecclesiastical and civil, often fall into sin like other men; and without repentance and forgiveness, in the way that God has provided and made known, they will perish.

entries.title: Leviticus 4:35
segments: Pardon of all transgressions is as free to the common people, to the poor and despised, as to the rich and the great.
